speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing your history. To better understand your symptoms, can you describe the exact location and nature of the shooting pain in your ear? Additionally, have you noticed any drainage or hearing changes since your tympanoplasty?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Myofascial pain of the auriculotemporal nerve (referred otalgia secondary to masticatory muscle spasm).

The shooting pain triggered by chewing and the tenderness with earrings strongly suggest referred pain from the muscles of mastication rather than a recurrence of the ear infection or graft failure. Have you noticed any jaw clicking, locking, or increased sensitivity when you press on the muscles in front of your ears?
